summary: K1 settles a uniqueness question that Kulaichev posed in 1984. Chiodo (C. R. Math. 2021) states in print that the question is still open, and the entry's quotations of that paper are accurate. The research audience can be named specifically: work on the geometry of the Śrī Yantra (Huet, Chiodo, Pustynski, Rao), certified computation in real algebraic geometry, and computer-assisted formal proof. The literature account is precise. It is open about its unread and non-peer-reviewed sources and claims no priority from them. Independent searching found no later work that answers the question.

internal_notes.evidence: Chiodo 2021, French text, section 'La recherche d'un unique śrīyantra' (p. 379 area)
internal_notes.message: Verified word for word: 'Il fournit un raisonnement qui indique l'existence d'une solution et il se pose la question (toujours ouverte) de l'unicité.' The entry reports this accurately. The page number the entry gives (p. 384) could not be confirmed from the extracted text: the passage appears in the early French section. This is a minor bibliographic point.

Verified: Kulaichev 'discusses whether the solution is unique (p. 285), estimates the complexity, and argues that the answer is out of reach. This problem is not considered here.' This supports both the claim that the question is open and the claim that the problem is hard. It is positive evidence that the result could support a paper.

internal_notes.evidence: Chiodo footnotes 7 and 19 against the Yantra.Kulaichev definition
internal_notes.message: Chiodo writes condition (b) as 'circumcircle of t1 coincides with E'. Read literally this would put t1's apex on the circle, which cannot happen for an inner triangle. The entry formalises (b) as 'base corners of t1 on the circle', the usual working reading. Condition (d), 'the incircle of t1 ∩ t5 is concentric with E', is encoded correctly as equal distance from (0,1/2) to t5's base and to t1's leg, with b4 < 1/2 < a0. Alignment belongs to the statement-alignment check. This is not a literature defect.

Admissibility (strictly ordered bases, positive half-widths, the set orientation, corners in the closed disc) restricts the claim to figures with the standard Śrī Yantra arrangement. That is the natural reading of Kulaichev's 'is the figure unique', and the entry openly says the condition is the submitter's own. It does not narrow the question beyond what Kulaichev meant. The account would be stronger if it said whether real solutions of Huet plus Kulaichev exist outside the admissible set; the earlier elimination census may already show this. This is for the statement-alignment check.

internal_notes.evidence: Rao 1998 (IJHS 33, 203-227), Tahta 1992 (Math. Gazette 76), Santhi et al. 2012, Tularam 2012 (Chiodo refs [20],[23],[21],[24])
internal_notes.message: The submitter says Rao 1998 was not read. Tahta, Santhi et al. and Tularam are not mentioned, though Chiodo groups them with Pustynski as works exploring the algebraic approach. I could not inspect them. Chiodo's 2021 statement that the question is still open comes after all of them, so they probably do not answer it. This is an evidence limitation, not an omission that changes the public account.

The PDF returned 404, so I could not check the entry's page-level quotations (Table 1 p. 274, the residual-plot uniqueness argument pp. 273-274, 'probably impossible' p. 275, and the degree bound of 12544). Search snippets agree with the reported degree bound and with Pustynski studying uniqueness numerically. The entry correctly presents his argument as numerical, not a proof.

A pre-registration describes classifying well-posed subsets of the Rao 1998 Śrī Yantra constraint system by certified affine-arithmetic Krawczyk box enumeration. I could not see its authors or date (HTTP 429). It may be related or overlapping work, possibly by the same submitter. A final account should check it and cite it if it is independent.

internal_notes.evidence: LeanCert (Lean 4 certified-numerics library with Krawczyk root certificates)
internal_notes.message: This is related tooling for formalisation. The entry does not say it was used. Citing it is optional unless code from it was used.

internal_notes.evidence: Prior Zenodo preprint by the same author (degree-348 minimal polynomial; degree-1744 resultant census)
internal_notes.message: The entry discloses this as non-peer-reviewed and makes no priority claim from it. That is acceptable. It means the Lean entry certifies a result the same author had already reached by other means; the kernel-checked certificate is the added value.

The 4 is earned but borderline. The question is real, stated in a peer-reviewed venue (C. R. Math.), and has stood since 1984. The audience is specialised: Śrī Yantra geometry is a small literature, mostly in IJHS. Interest beyond that comes from the computational side (certified real-root isolation for a hard polynomial system) and from formal proof. A 5 is not justified.

what_would_reach_higher: Read Rao 1998, Tahta 1992 and Santhi et al. 2012 and state briefly what each says, or does not say, about uniqueness under conditions (a)-(d)
Say whether the Huet plus Kulaichev equations have real solutions outside the admissible set, so the scope of 'unique' is fully transparent
Check the Synapse pre-registration on certified enumeration of the Rao system and cite it if it is independent
Confirm the Chiodo page references (the French passage appears earlier than p. 384) and Pustynski's page-level quotations against inspectable copies
Get the earlier uniqueness census or degree-348 polynomial peer-reviewed, or formalise the minimal polynomial, so outside evidence of interest backs the result
Name the intended audiences explicitly in the account (Śrī Yantra geometry, certified real algebraic geometry, formal proof)
